findings.title: canManage() grants manage on view-only permission
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the fallback check is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` — it treats the VIEW scope as sufficient for manage. An administrator who only has an all-groups permission with the `view` scope (and no manage-users role) will have canManage() return true. This is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (requireManage()) to authorize creating top-level groups, so a view-only admin can create (and, via the same check elsewhere, potentially modify) groups. The VIEW scope should be removed from this check; only MANAGE should satisfy canManage().

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authz resource ID instead of group ID
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the callback calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. However, hasPermission(groupId, ...) looks the resource up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, and in the V2 schema the resource *name* is the group ID (set by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource), while resource.getId() is the internal authorization-resource UUID. Passing the UUID means findByName never matches the specific group resource (it silently falls back to the all-groups resource), and the returned set contains authz resource IDs rather than group IDs. This set is consumed by UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource as the UserModel.GROUPS filter and by getUsersCount, so admins whose user visibility comes from group view-members/manage-members permissions will get wrong (empty) user lists and counts. It should use `groupResource.getName()` in both places.

findings.title: Per-group resources created without resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates resources via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, ...)` and updates scopes, but never calls `resource.setType(...)` (unlike the V1 group permissions which set type "Group", and unlike init() which sets the type on the all-resources). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() queries `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`; per-group resources created through this path have a null type and will never be returned by that query, so group-specific view-members permissions are ignored when computing the groups with view permission.

findings.title: No upgrade path for realms that already have an admin-permissions client
findings.body: The Groups resource type, its all-groups resource, and the new scopes (manage-membership, manage-members, view-members) are only created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init(), which runs only when the admin-permissions client is first created for a realm. Realms that enabled admin permissions before this change already have the client, so init() returns early and the "Groups" resource and group scopes never exist. In that state GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` with `resource` being null (getResourceTypeResource returns null), causing a NullPointerException on any group permission evaluation, and getOrCreateResource for a Groups resource would fail with ModelException("No scopes found."). A migration/update path for existing admin-permissions clients is needed.
